findings.title: The recovery audit does not preserve the falsely claimed reviewer identity.
findings.verbatim_body: The current state correctly has `review_assignment: null` and `design_review: pending`, but the clearing transition records only an identical operator-constraints replacement. It never records the removed `operator:planning-1-assignment` value or old/new approval state. This loses the exact historical fact the recovery is supposed to preserve.

findings.title: “Atomic” cross-card replacement has no implementable transaction contract.
findings.verbatim_body: The design lists multiple semantic replacements but does not define validation-before-write, staging, commit order, rollback/crash recovery, or consistency across six values files, rendered cards, index projections, and both audit representations. An implementation could partially update the packet while nominally satisfying the prose.

findings.title: Request-root and cwd safety are unspecified despite the absolute live #114 fixture path.
findings.verbatim_body: The design does not require canonical root resolution, containment checks, symlink rejection, issue/path identity checks, or copying the golden fixture into an isolated temporary root before mutation tests. “Read-only” alone does not prevent a malformed request or cwd mistake from modifying #114.

findings.title: Graph validation is fixture-specific rather than a general recovery contract.
findings.verbatim_body: The design hard-codes `#276 -> #277 -> #278 -> parent` without defining a typed graph input, node roles, edge orientation, integration ownership, or how generic decomposed issues are validated. The exact chain belongs in the #114 golden test; the product route needs general invariants, including a defined rejection rule for trust redefinition.

findings.title: The semantic replacement surface is incomplete and ambiguous relative to the live issue.
findings.verbatim_body: The live contract includes SIP operator constraints, SPP risks/replan triggers/affected areas, and VPP preparation lanes when needed. The design explicitly names identity, STP, SPP steps/unspecified “selected planning fields,” SRP, and SOR, leaving implementers unable to determine the complete allowed field set. It also does not state that shared identity must be updated consistently across every card.

findings.title: The validation plan does not explicitly cover all required invariants.
findings.verbatim_body: Its focused lane summarizes broad categories, but does not name negative bootstrap-overwrite proof, request-root/cwd and symlink safety, exact one-entry audit consistency, failure atomicity, or preservation of already-repaired fields unless intentionally superseded.

limitations: This was a read-only packet/design review.
The reviewer inspected issue #291’s supplied cards, index, audit, design, diagram, and live issue body.
The reviewer did not inspect implementation code, mutate or execute against #114, run validators, or verify the external fixture and pinned origin/main SHA.
The supplied record identity itself matched generation 4 and digest 8a268aedefe688ab543b2265f79ac0037590efef2c97e3f8753416255b559b20; branch/worktree were null and approval remained pending.
